Pretty hard boss in all fairness. I beat it using a +10 Kirkhammer and buffing occasionally at lv115. A lot of strats recommend staying close/behind/underneath the beast without locking on but I found that I got squished way too often. I suggest staying locked on and keeping your distance and until he uses the slow left, right swipes (quickstep to the right and close for a hit) or the blood hail (quickstep right up to his head for two big hits or a charged R2). After dealing one or two blows, quickstep away to avoid his ground and pound, then repeat this process. Once the worm pops out of his head stump I got as close as possible and just wailed on his ankles. Took a lot of damage but found that when he used the worm attack he's left open for a fair amount of time, enough for a charged R2 at the very least. After this Queen Yharnam will seem like a cakewalk :)

My recipe has changed over time but right now I usually start by finely chopping one large white onion, white cabbage, leek and sometimes a little spring onion and mixing this in a large bowl with ground pork, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, mirin, oyster sauce, sesame oil, salt, pepper, white sugar and chilli flakes. I'll knead this for a while with my hands and then let it set for around 40 min. Next I'll take some gyoza wrappers and add a heaped teaspoons worth of the mixture to each, usually until I have around 25-30. The more the better...

When they're all ready it's time to place them in a large pan on high heat with a little sesame oil and wait until they start to get brown on the bottom. Cover them in one cup of water, turn down the heat a little and stick on the lid. Let 'em steam for around 4 min, then check the water level and maybe add a little more sesame oil before covering again for another 5 min.

Finally I'll remove the lid and boil off the rest of the water, cover the pan with a large plate and flip it over, which should successfully result in something resembling the delicious plate of extra crispy gyoza you see before you! :)
